messages:
Jordan (AcmePay): Hey team, customer reported rerank endpoint returning different scores for identical inputs after the recent model rollout. They sent a minimal repro: same query + same candidate set, previously candidate A had score 0.82 > B 0.47, now B 0.76 > A 0.50. :confused:
Priya (CS): Ugh, thanks. Do we have the request-id or example payload from the customer? any error codes?
Jordan (AcmePay): They included the exact curl and response. No 5xxs, just score differences. Request-ID: req_20260310_42. Payload (they redacted user ids):
```json
{
  "model": "redwood/rerank-compact:2026-03-09",
  "query": "best wireless headphones for running",
  "candidates": ["Bose Sport Earbuds", "Sony WF-SP800N", "Jabra Elite Active"],
  "normalize": true
}
```
Alex (ML Eng): Thanks. Which model variant did we roll out on 2026-03-09? Was that the new tokenizer-normalization patch or just kernel selection?
Ravi (Runtime): That rollout enabled whitespace-preserving tokenization fallback + a new attention kernel for longer contexts. Rollout id: rollout-2026-03-09-rk. We did a gradual canary (5% -> 25%) but I think some Dedicated customers got it pinned by assignment rule.
Sam (Eng-Infra): ops-bot alerted on a small bump in score-variance for rerank endpoints at ~2026-03-09 18:12 UTC. (auto)
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: rerank.score_variance increased 3.4x for region-us-east-1 between 2026-03-09 17:50 and 18:30. Link: https://console.redwood/alerts/54321
Priya (CS): Jordan can you ask the customer to run this exact curl and paste the full response (scores + headers)? also ask them to try with leading/trailing whitespace trimmed vs preserved. Quick curl:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/rerank-compact:2026-03-09","query":"best wireless headphones for running","candidates":["Bose Sport Earbuds","Sony WF-SP800N","Jabra Elite Active"],"normalize":true}'
```
Jordan (AcmePay): Will do. Customer said they didn't change inputs. They also tried pinning to previous model tag `redwood/rerank-compact:2026-02-22` and got the old scores back. So likely model/tokenization change.
Alex (ML Eng): That matches a tokenization normalization difference hypothesis. If tokenization splits differently, reranker features change and score ordering can flip even if text identical at surface-level. Can you get their raw bytes (maybe there's non-breaking spaces or weird unicode)?
Priya (CS): Also confirm they didn't hit any request-size limits or candidate ordering transforms on our side. Any pre-processing changes in the route?
Ravi (Runtime): No route-level changes. We did toggle a `preserve_ws` flag in tokenizer code path for the rollout to improve prefix-caching behavior — that could change token offsets. I'll pull logs for req_20260310_42.
Sam (Eng-Infra): I can pin AcmePay's tenant to the previous model tag for now (short-term hotfix). Need confirmation from CS to proceed.
Priya (CS): Please pin — customer is in pilot and this is causing user-facing regressions. Jordan -> confirm with customer they're ok with a model pin while we investigate.
Jordan (AcmePay): Customer agreed to temporary pin. Please proceed.
Ravi (Runtime): Pinning now -> applied model override for tenant acmepay-prod to redwood/rerank-compact:2026-02-22. Ops note: this will route their rerank calls to older serving pool, TTL 48h unless extended.
Alex (ML Eng): Meanwhile I'll run our rerank regression harness comparing 2026-02-22 vs 2026-03-09 across the canonical evaluation set and also reproduce with exact bytes from the customer once we get them. If we confirm tokenizer normalization is root cause, fix options: revert tokenizer change, add compatibility mode, or introduce deterministic normalization that keeps legacy behavior behind a flag.
Priya (CS): Action items: 1) Jordan: get full response + raw request bytes + confirm pin ok (assigned). 2) Ravi/Sam: pin completed (in progress/done). 3) Alex: run regression harness and report deltas. 4) CS to update customer with ETA and workaround.
Jordan (AcmePay): I'll post the customer's raw payload + response once I have it. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Priya (CS): Also upload req_20260310_42 logs to the incident bucket and tag with "rerank-tokenization".
Ravi (Runtime): Done -> logs uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/req_20260310_42.log.
Alex (ML Eng): I already see small token offset diffs for that query in the canary model run locally. Early guess: whitespace-preserve changed token boundaries around "running" vs " running". That suffices to change rerank features. Will post a short reproducible snippet shortly.
Jordan (AcmePay): Posting the customer's response now (sanitized):
```json
{
  "scores": [0.50, 0.76, 0.62],
  "candidates": ["Bose Sport Earbuds","Sony WF-SP800N","Jabra Elite Active"]
}
```
Priya (CS): Thanks. For the customer message I'll say: we've pinned your workspace to the prior model, this should restore previous behavior immediately. We're investigating a tokenizer change introduced in the recent rollout and will follow up with a permanent fix.
Sam (Eng-Infra): Pin complete and confirmed via routing logs.
Alex (ML Eng): Follow-up: reproduction script I run shows same flip when input contains Unicode non-breaking space (0xC2A0). Recommend adding a normalization step in our preprocessing to normalize NBSP to regular space for rerank pipeline unless we intentionally want the distinction.
Priya (CS): Good call. Please open a PR for normalization + add a regression test covering this exact example.
Alex (ML Eng): Will do. PR and eval report expected by EOD.
Jordan (AcmePay): Customer notified and confirmed scores back to expected after pin. Closing loop on customer side.
Priya (CS): Keeping thread open until PR merged and we have a postmortem note. Thanks everyone. :sparkles:
